title: docs(spec): reconcile the RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR Lifecycle docblock with check (b3)
body:
Part of #18624 — item ① only; the card stays open for the half named below.

Clause-②: no

`RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR`'s docblock is shipped text: it reaches consumers in `@objectstack/spec`'s `dist/index.d.ts`, measured by grepping the built `.d.ts` for a phrase from this very paragraph against a positive control. Since check (b3) landed, two of its sentences were false, and one of them contradicted a remedy the gate prints.

## What was false

| docblock said | check (b3) does |
|:---|:---|
| 「The one state the gate rejects is an entry naming a key that is still LIVE」 | rejects a **second** state — a NESTED row whose def this build emits but whose dotted path it does not |
| 「Entries are permanent」 | its refusal text ends `… or delete the entry from packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` |
| 「its entry here stays, and then names a key the build no longer emits — the expected steady state, not an error」 | true only for a TOP-LEVEL key; a nested row never reaches `authorable-surface/` at all, so it has no aging clock and can never be in that steady state |

An author following the docblock would not delete the row; an author following the gate would. Both texts ship in the same repository, so two people each doing as they were told go opposite ways.

## What changed

One file, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`, comment text only — the hand-written docblock above the declaration, outside the `os-generated` regions (`check:migration-registry` green confirms nothing generated moved).

- The `## Lifecycle` paragraph scopes the aging-out steady state to a **top-level** tombstone and says why a nested row can never be in it.
- It lists **both** rejected states with the check that owns each and the remedy that check actually prints: still-LIVE is check (b2), nested-and-unresolvable is check (b3).
- It states the routing rule that decides which check judges a row — a row is read as a path only when its `name` half carries a dot **and** this build emits no top-level property of that exact name, so a live dotted top-level key such as the OData context key stays on the map check (b2) has always judged it on. That mirrors `build-schemas.ts`'s `!currentKeys.has(k) && isNestedAuthorableKey(k)` routing rather than paraphrasing it as "has a dot".
- It reconciles permanence with deletion instead of leaving the two to contradict: a row that was ever TRUE of some build is history and is never deleted; a row check (b2) or (b3) refuses was never true of any build, so deleting it removes a false claim rather than a record.
- It repeats check (b3)'s own ⛔ — that check cannot yet tell a wrong row apart from every truthful one, and for the shapes its refusal enumerates the remedy is to teach the check, never to delete a row that is telling the truth.
- The `## What reads it` bullet for check (b) and the `@see` roster name check (b3), which reads this table and was named by neither.

⛔ No gate behaviour moves. No schema, export, registry entry or refusal condition is touched; the set of metadata that validates is byte-for-byte what it was. The changeset is a `patch` because the shipped `.d.ts` text moves, not because anything executes differently.

## Sweep — the other carriers of the same sentences

Checked before editing, since fixing one carrier and leaving three is the failure mode this card is an instance of:

- `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR`'s parallel `## Lifecycle` paragraph in the same file carries nearly identical wording. It is **still true** and is deliberately untouched: check (b3) judges nested KEYS, and that table's only consumer remains the manifest deletion gate.
- `packages/spec/scripts/lib/nested-authorable-keys.ts` already states the three-state distinction correctly and at length; nothing there is stale.
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md` describes the entry-file layout only and makes no lifecycle claim.
- No test, generated doc or `content/docs/` page quotes the paragraph: the phrases 「Entries are permanent」 and 「The one state the gate rejects」 occur in this file and nowhere else in the tree.

## What is deliberately NOT in this PR

The card carries three items; this delivers item ① and no more, which is why the first line reads Part of rather than binding a closing keyword to the card.

- **Item ②** — check (b3)'s refusal enumerates two legitimate shapes it cannot tell apart from a wrong row, and a third exists (an ancestor of a registered nested key tombstoned in place, removed via the guidance route, or reached through a `$ref` to a tombstoned `$def`). Re-measured here and structurally real: a tombstoned ancestor node renders as `{ "not": {} }`, which carries no `properties`, so any registered descendant path under it lands in the same `unresolvable` state. It is unreached on this tree. Its carrier is the refusal text in `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts`, **outside this PR's declared file surface** (`packages/spec/src/migrations/**` plus any sibling test pinning the wording), and writing a new enumerated shape is authored prose rather than a mechanical repair — so it is reported rather than taken here.
- **Item ③** — re-measured first-hand and confirmed: `packages/spec/scripts/lib/nested-authorable-keys.ts` contains `items` 4 times and `prefixItems` 0 times, so a tuple-shaped nested row would not be seen. The card records this as a limit of sight rather than a defect and asks for no action.

## Verification

All readings taken in a dedicated worktree at head `f75798a2`, after merging `origin/main`.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` — exit 0; 34/34 declaration files present.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — exit 0; **all 15** generated artifacts up to date, `check:migration-registry` among them.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — exit 0 (includes `check:scripts-typecheck` and `check:test-typecheck`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — exit 0; **488 test files, 14182 tests passed**.
- `pnpm lint` (the repo-wide union, `eslint . --no-inline-config`) — exit 0, re-run on this exact head after the merge, 71s.
- Gate families derived mechanically from the change set with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, re-derived after the changeset existed and again after the merge, then reconciled with `--ran`: **78 derived, 75 run green, 3 NOT MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.**

Every exit code was captured before any pipe. The three NOT MEASURED are all `exit 3` = PREREQUISITE NOT MET, which is neither a pass nor a failure:

- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — needs a whole-repo `pnpm build` (87 packages have no `dist/`).
- `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure` — needs `@objectstack/objectql` built.
- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` — its positive-control fixture is pinned to a commit this shallow checkout cannot reach; the gate's non-self-test run was green. This one grades the checker's fixtures, not this diff.

CI covers all three. No reverse-verification or ablation run is reported because none is owed: this diff adds no gate, changes no cross-package type, and has no behaviour whose removal could turn a test red.

## Acceptance notes

- `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` §3 warns a retirement author only about check (b2) ("⚠ **不要**在墓碑落地前先加条目") and never mentions check (b3). That is **incomplete, not false** — no sentence there is contradicted — so by the filing rule it is noted rather than filed. Carrier: a governed surface, outside this card's file surface. Whoever picks up item ② is the natural taker, since that is the next edit to touch (b3)'s author-facing text.
